reason: The filter picture shows blood entering its capillaries and small substances crossing into the surrounding space.
expectation: The filter will separate water and other small substances from blood cells and large proteins.

alternatives.reason: The ureters also visibly fit the kidney-to-bladder route, which can be built first.

effect: The filtered fluid contains useful glucose and water as well as wastes, so it needs the recovery tube next.
reaction: It is interesting that the filter lets useful substances through too.
reason: The recovery tube picture shows glucose, some salts and much water returning to blood.
expectation: Useful substances will move back into the blood, leaving fluid to continue toward the urine route.

alternatives.reason: I could build the drainage route first instead.

effect: The recovery tube returned useful substances and much water to the blood, leaving urine. Next I need to build its route to the bladder.
reaction: It makes sense now why filtering alone is not enough.
reason: The urinary system has an empty ureter slot, and the tubes lead from the kidneys toward the bladder.
expectation: The ureters will attach to the kidneys' drainage outlets.

alternatives.reason: The bladder also has a named slot and could be fitted first.

effect: The ureters now connect the kidney outlets toward the bladder position; the bladder still needs fitting.
reaction: The arrows make it clear that the tubes move urine with muscular squeezes.
reason: The bladder fits the remaining named slot and completes the route from the kidneys.
expectation: The bladder will attach below the ureters to receive urine.

effect: The bladder completes the continuous route from the kidneys through the ureters, and both goals are complete.
reaction: The unchanged fluid trail made the route easy to follow.

mostWorthwhile.text: Filtering blood and then recovering useful substances was most worthwhile: it showed why the kidney cannot simply remove everything that passes through its filter.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the bladder was the least challenging part because its named slot made the choice obvious, though it completed the route.

surprise.text: I was surprised that useful glucose and water pass through the filter along with wastes and must be recovered.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary; the pictures and named slots gave each one a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter to see how another body system works, although the slot-fitting here was fairly predictable.
